alex (customer): hitting intermittent 401s + high latency on mobile this morning, any quick way to grab traces so you can look?
jen (Support): sorry about that — can you grab any request IDs shown in the SDK response or the server logs? saves a lot of time. :pray:
alex (customer): where do I look in the iOS SDK? I only see a generic error in the callback
jen (Support): in iOS Swift, the completion returns (result, meta, error). meta.requestId or meta["request_id"] is usually present. also check console logs if you enabled SDK logging.
jen (Support): quick iOS snippet:
jen (Support): ```swift
RedwoodClient.shared.enableLogging = true
RedwoodClient.shared.generate(prompt: "hi") { result, meta, error in
  print("requestId:", meta?['request_id'] ?? meta?['requestId'] ?? "none")
}
```
alex (customer): thanks — where for Android and web?
samir (SRE): Android (Kotlin): Response has `requestId` on the result object; or look in logcat: `adb logcat | grep Redwood` and grep for `request_id`.
maya (DevEx): Web/JS: the REST response has header `x-request-id` and the JSON response sometimes contains `request_id`. Example curl to reproduce (replace <KEY>):
maya (DevEx): ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"test"}'
# Look for "x-request-id:" in the response headers or "request_id" in the body
```
alex (customer): I tried curl and only saw `x-request-id: 01F...` in headers — is that enough?
jen (Support): perfect, that header is the one we need. please paste the full header value and the approximate timestamp (UTC) when you hit the error.
alex (customer): okay: x-request-id: 01F3B2KZQ0Y9W1A23 — happened ~2026-02-28T14:12:05Z
samir (SRE): great — can you also tell us the route (generate/chat/embeddings), model, and whether it was streaming? streaming sometimes uses a different trace path.
alex (customer): route=chat, model=rwd-4c, streaming=false
jen (Support): if you're using Redwood Console you can also: Console -> Requests -> set time window -> search for that request id -> download debug bundle (redwood-debug.zip). that bundle has server logs + kernel selection + full trace ids we can use to correlate.
alex (customer): how do I download the debug bundle? I only see request details
maya (DevEx): open the request detail, top-right click "Download debug bundle". if you don't see it, give me your org id and I'll enable it for the workspace temporarily.
alex (customer): org is org_7x9
jen (Support): two more asks: 1) please redact any user PII before uploading logs (or remove full prompts). 2) include the SDK version + region you hit (us-east-1 / eu-west-1) — headers sometimes include `x-region`.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-345 (linked to this thread)
samir (SRE): once we have the header + time window + debug bundle we can correlate backend trace id -> GPU node -> scheduling logs. thanks for sending those values.
alex (customer): uploaded debug bundle to the ticket and pasted the header value in the ticket now — let me know if you need anything else
jen (Support): received and triaging. if we need live repro we'll ask for a short curl with `--trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt` so we can capture full wire logs. example:
jen (Support): ```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-4c","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"test"}]}' \
  --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt
# attach /tmp/trace.txt to the ticket
```
maya (DevEx): if any of this is sensitive, paste only the request id and timestamp and say "logs attached to ticket". our SREs can pull logs from our side with the request id.
jen (Support): ETA for initial triage ~30–45m. we'll post updates here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
alex (customer): awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
jen (Support): marking follow-up tasks in the ticket and closing the loop in 45m unless we need more info.
